title: URL Patterns API
excerpt: Define routes with the urls() builder function.
content:
The urls() function accepts a builder callback that receives helpers like path, layout, include, and parallel. Each helper creates a route definition that the router evaluates at request time.

## path()

Defines a route that matches a URL pattern. The handler receives a context object with params, request, and reverse.

## layout()

Wraps child routes in a shared UI shell. The layout renders an Outlet where matched children appear.

title: Response Types
excerpt: Return JSON, text, markdown, and other formats from routes.
content:
Response routes skip the RSC pipeline and return raw data. Use path.json() for JSON APIs, path.text() for plain text, path.md() for markdown, and path.xml() for XML responses.

## Content Negotiation

When a path has both an RSC handler and a response handler, the router negotiates based on the Accept header. Browsers get HTML, API clients get JSON.
